system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The labels “[STANDARD]”, “cleared” and “settled” are Seller assertions only and do not evidence Buyer approval. No Amelia Frost approval has been given for any fallback position.

| ID | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**; 20% is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft. | **Reject and mark up to 25% / AUD 6m** — the proposed fallback is not authorised merely because the Seller has included it. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 aggregate basket; Seller liable only for the excess. | **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially reduces recovery through much higher thresholds and a deductible basket. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general claims; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval; separate periods for other claim categories. | **Reject and require 24 months** — the 18-month fallback is unauthorised and the “all Claims” override would collapse separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity.” | Separate **100% cap**, limitation period of at least **six years**, and exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject and insert a separate Fundamental/Title regime** — ownership, authority and capacity risks must not be diluted by general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no adequate express fraud carve-out is identified. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Non-negotiably add the full carve-out** — the Buyer cannot waive this protection under the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only **specific, fair disclosure** in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no deemed disclosure through data-room availability, public searches or prudent enquiry. | **Delete clauses 1.1–1.2 as general disclosure and assess each specific disclosure warranty-by-warranty** — mere document availability does not fairly disclose its consequences. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion and all constructive/imputed knowledge; any permitted knowledge mechanism must be tightly defined and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Seller warranty knowledge qualifiers should use named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry. | **Delete the proposed qualifier** — it improperly shifts diligence and disclosure risk to the Buyer and converts discoverability into deemed knowledge. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met. | An **effective consent** plus evidence that every associated condition is satisfied, each obtained before Completion and in form and substance satisfactory to Buyer. | **Make this a strict unsatisfied condition precedent, not reasonable endeavours or consent-on-delivery** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and conditional consent may be ineffective. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. | **Reject a post-Completion release and require payout-and-release mechanics at Completion** — any deferred release would require an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are said to be a Seller matter but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unquantified. | Express Seller funding or a separate Completion funds-flow line item for **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Revise the funds flow and allocate the full amount to Seller** — omission creates a risk that the Company/Buyer bears a Completion-triggered liability outside the price mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, without independent verification. | A broader indemnity covering payment, ownership/transfer failure, infringement, remediation and resulting loss, while preserving the contractual SOW3 payment cure and verification process. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify the AUD 180,000 before fixing any payment mechanism** — paying the fee may cure transfer conditions but does not by itself address all chain-of-title and loss risks. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure does not establish access, exact scope, notification duty, loss or a confirmed breach. | Preservation of logs and evidence, prompt investigation, ongoing Buyer updates, access to findings, and appropriate pre-Completion remediation/cooperation obligations. | **Require investigation covenants and reserve rights without asserting a breach or amount** — the evidence is incomplete, so neither materiality nor absence of liability is presently established. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, AUD 330,000 total, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Determine timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability before deciding treatment; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Keep treatment open pending diligence and prevent commitment without Buyer consent** — the disclosure does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller proposes limitations applying to all Claims and treats Tax/IP as settled within the general regime. | Separate regimes for **Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants**, with no hidden general limitation override. | **Rewrite the limitation hierarchy and category-specific rules expressly** — an “all Claims” formulation could unintentionally cap or time-bar protections negotiated separately. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the internal Company share register at DD-012 as evidence of 100% ownership. | Independent evidence of ownership, valid issuance, authority and absence/release of encumbrances, including appropriate corporate, PPSR and transaction-specific checks and Completion deliverables. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive; complete independent verification** — a supplied internal register identifies the asserted holder but is not independent proof of good, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller asserts Tax and IP warranties are settled under the proposed general regime. | Treat both regimes as **open**, with scope, caps, periods, exclusions and indemnities separately negotiated; assume neither unlimited liability nor agreement. | **Reject the “settled” characterisation and reserve all positions** — no Buyer authority or substantive agreement supports folding Tax and IP into the general regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
